advances: Realized support paths at smooth strictly positively curved compatible families. The original compatible gaps may vanish.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The curvatures and widths have uniform positive lower bounds on the finite family and compact sphere. For small parameters the displayed paths are $C^2$-close to $h_p$ and preserve both bounds. Indeed $H_p$ is $C^2$ off zero, and $u+tZ(u)$ stays in a compact annulus. The perturbed homogeneous extension has positive semidefinite Hessian off zero: the tangential block is $Q/|x|$ and the radial part vanishes. On a line through zero, positive width makes the left derivative no larger than the right derivative. Convexity on lines gives convexity of the extension, hence it is a support function. Uniformly close support functions preserve any fixed smaller ball inside each old body.

The same $u+tZ(u)$ is used at all bases, preserving every homogeneous support inequality. The affine-in-base term has zero change of gap because both the barycentric sum and base mean are fixed. For each $u$, the scalar map $F_u(z,s)=s-t\sum_a\chi_a(u)\phi_a(z,s)$ is jointly concave and nondecreasing in $s$ over the relevant data for small nonnegative $t$, by a uniform bound on the partial derivatives of the $\phi_a$. The data and convex combinations used in this argument lie in a small common convex neighborhood of the original compact convex hull. Thus
$
F_u(q,g_q)\ge F_u(q,\sum_p\alpha_pg_p)\ge\sum_p\alpha_pF_u(p,g_p).
$
These are the anchored support inequalities. Every point of the canonical hull over a sampled base groups into an anchored combination of sampled fibers, so those inequalities give the exact sections. The projection is $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. Finally $\nabla H_p(u)=x_p(u)$ and differentiating in $t$ gives $\dot h_p$ with uniform support remainder $o(t)$.

The old support extension is differentiable away from zero, so every exposed face is a singleton. Moreover no point can have two distinct normals: two nonopposite normals would give a whole arc of normals with the same exposed point and hence a zero derivative along that arc, contrary to $Q_p>0$. Opposite normals at one point would violate positive width. Thus the inverse Gauss map parametrizes the whole old boundary with unique normals.

For the volume derivative, fix an interior point $o_p$ and use the radial distance $r_t(e)$ in direction $e$ from $o_p$ to the new boundary. It is the minimum of $(h_p(t,u)-u\cdot o_p)/(u\cdot e)$ over $u\cdot e>0$. All minimizing directions have denominator bounded below uniformly, since the bodies contain a fixed ball about $o_p$ and lie in a fixed ball. At $t=0$ the minimizing direction is the unique outward normal $u$ at $o_p+r_0(e)e$. Minimizers for $t\to0$ converge to it by compactness and uniform support convergence. Comparing the old and new minimizing directions in the difference quotient gives $r'_0(e)=\dot h_p(u)/(u\cdot e)$, with a uniform bound on the quotient. For $dS$ on the old surface the radial Jacobian is $r_0(e)^{d-1}/(u\cdot e)$. Differentiating the signed radial layer integral by domination gives $\int\dot h_p\,dS$. The inverse Gauss parametrization has tangent differential $Q_p$, so $dS=J_p(u)\,du$.

For a fixed cap the same layer integral includes its indicator. At a proper plane, the portion of the old boundary in that plane lies in the relative boundary of the section and has zero surface measure. At a supporting plane strict convexity makes the intersection at most one point, again surface-null for $d\ge2$. Thus the limiting indicator along the thin signed layer exists almost everywhere and gives the fixed cap formula. For the threshold displacement, integrate the perturbed parallel section areas between the old and new threshold. They converge to the old section area along any sequence of such levels and parameters. For a proper old section this is proper section continuity (d4e455a28be6cde4). At an old supporting plane all section points approach the unique old support point by compactness, so their $(d-1)$-areas converge to zero. Strictly exterior levels stay exterior. This proves the joint derivative for both available signs.

statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let a nonempty finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ carry positive convex bodies $K_p$ with $C^2$ supports $h_p$ on the unit sphere. Assume $Q_p=\nabla_S^2h_p+h_pI$ is everywhere positive definite and $h_q(u)\ge\sum_p\alpha_ph_p(u)$ for every $u$ whenever $q=\sum_p\alpha_pp\in P$, $\alpha_p\ge0$, $\sum_p\alpha_p=1$. Let $H_p$ be the homogeneous support extension. Take $C^2$ spherical functions $\psi_0,\ldots,\psi_n$, a $C^2$ vector field $Z$ into $\mathbb R^d$, and a finite list of $C^2$ spherical functions $\chi_a\ge0$ and smooth convex functions $\phi_a(z,s)$ on a neighborhood of the convex hull of the compact support data $(p,h_p(u))$. Put
$
g_p(t,u)=H_p(u+tZ(u))+t\bigl(\psi_0(u)+\sum_l p_l\psi_l(u)\bigr),\qquad
h_p(t,u)=g_p(t,u)-t\sum_a\chi_a(u)\phi_a(p,g_p(t,u)).
$
These are supports of positive compatible fibers for sufficiently small $t\ge0$, and for both signs when the list of contractions is empty. With only the affine-in-base additions every old gap stays exactly unchanged. The canonical hull realizes the perturbed fibers at all $P$, and its lattice trace has exactly those bases if $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$.

Put $x_p(u)=\nabla_Sh_p(u)+h_p(u)u$, $J_p(u)=\det Q_p(u)$, and $\dot h_p=x_p\cdot Z+\psi_0+\sum_l p_l\psi_l-\sum_a\chi_a\phi_a(p,h_p)$. For $M(t)=\sum_p|K_p(t)|$ and any fixed nonvertical cap $H=\{(p,x):a\cdot p+v\cdot x\ge b\}$ with $\|v\|=1$, the total mass derivative is $\sum_p\int\dot h_pJ_p\,du$ and the fixed cap derivative is $\sum_p\int\dot h_pJ_p\mathbf1_H(p,x_p(u))\,du$. Jointly changing $b$ to $b+ts$ subtracts $s\sum_p\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_p\cap\{v\cdot x=b-a\cdot p\})$ from the latter derivative. All derivatives are along the available signs.
title: Actual Gauss-localized support deformations and their cap derivatives
